title: A Variational Framework for Time-Dependent Quantum Systems with Applications to Floquet Hamiltonians
authors: Ibsal Assi, Meenu Kumari, J. P. F. LeBlanc
abstract: We introduce a variational framework for approximating the time-evolution operator $\hat{U}(t)$ within a physically motivated operator manifold, reformulating quantum dynamics as a tractable problem in operator space using stationary action principle. For periodically driven systems, the resulting approximate evolution operator directly yields an effective Floquet Hamiltonian, offering a non-perturbative alternative to conventional expansion-based methods. The framework is systematically improvable by enlarging the operator pool and naturally incorporates symmetries and physical constraints. When the operator manifold is chosen from the terms of a truncated Magnus expansion, the variational procedure effectively resums the Magnus series within the restricted space, significantly enhancing accuracy. We benchmark the approach on the driven Rabi model, the driven Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model, and the one-dimensional driven Ising chain, yielding effective Floquet Hamiltonians that are systematically more accurate than low-order Magnus expansions, particularly in regimes where the latter converge poorly, and illustrating applicability to systems with exponentially large Hilbert spaces. Although we focus here on Floquet systems, the formalism applies equally to generic time-dependent Hamiltonians, providing a versatile tool for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
summary: The paper introduces a variational framework to accurately approximate the time evolution of quantum systems, particularly those subjected to periodic driving (Floquet systems). By minimizing an action principle on a constrained operator manifold, it derives effective Floquet Hamiltonians that surpass the accuracy limits of standard Magnus expansions. This method offers a versatile and scalable tool for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics across various physical models.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a systematic variational framework for approximating the time-evolution operator of general time-dependent quantum systems, with a specific focus on deriving effective Floquet Hamiltonians for periodically driven systems.
main_result: The proposed variational method yields an effective Floquet Hamiltonian that is systematically more accurate than low-order Magnus expansions, especially in regimes where conventional methods fail to converge.
method: It reformulates quantum dynamics using a variational principle applied to the action integral over a parameterized operator manifold. This leads to solving coupled ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for the variational parameters.
model_or_system: The framework is general, applying to any time-dependent Hamiltonian H(t). Benchmarking was performed on specific models like the driven Rabi model and the driven Ising chain, which are representative of periodically driven quantum systems.
key_observables: The effective Floquet Hamiltonian (H_F) and the variational parameters {theta_j(t)} that define the approximate time-evolution operator U(t).
important_parameters: Period T (for periodic driving), the size of the chosen operator manifold M, and the convergence behavior relative to the Magnus expansion order.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of a physically motivated, finite-dimensional operator manifold spanned by $\{\hat{O}_j\}$ that can parameterize the time evolution. The accuracy depends on the completeness of this chosen basis set.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the entire variational framework, mapping from input Hamiltonian H(t) and basis operators to the output effective Floquet Hamiltonian H_F.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the variational action principle for U(t), derives the coupled ODEs governing the parameters on the operator manifold, details how this approach scales by projecting dynamics onto the low-dimensional operator space, and benchmarks the method against established techniques like the Magnus expansion and flow equations using specific physical models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-perturbative tool for analyzing open quantum systems and periodically driven matter. Its ability to systematically improve accuracy over standard expansions makes it highly valuable for simulating complex dynamics in condensed matter or AMO settings where high precision is required.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic illustration of the variational framework. Given a time-periodic Hamiltonian ˆH(t) and a physically motivated pool of operators { ˆOj}, we construct a variational ansatz ˆUA(θ(t)) = e−i ˆ A(θ(t)). The action S is optimized to obtain the equations of motion for the variational parameters θ(t). After numerical integration yields the approximate propagator ˆUA(θ(T)) = e−i ˆ A(θ(T )). If the Hamiltonian is periodic, ˆH(t + T) = ˆH(t), the Floquet Hamiltonian is extracted as ˆHF = ˆA(θ(T))/T
